title: Serialize And Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Design a `Codec` with `serialize(root) -> str` and `deserialize(data) -> root` such that `deserialize(serialize(root))` rebuilds exactly the original tree, including its shape and values. The string format is entirely up to you, but negative values and the empty tree must work, and the two methods must not depend on shared state.

examples.output: a string s such that deserialize(s) is the same tree
empty tree round-trips to an empty tree

hints: A traversal alone is ambiguous unless it also records where children are missing.
Do a preorder traversal and write an explicit marker for every empty child. Pick a delimiter between tokens.
To decode, split on the delimiter and consume tokens in order with a pointer: a marker returns None, otherwise create a node and recursively build its left then its right.

input.$py: [x for i in range(1,3000) for x in (i,None)]+[3000]
[3000]+[x for i in range(2999,0,-1) for x in (i,None)][:-1]

solution.explanation: Serialize with a preorder DFS, writing each value or a marker such as 'N' for an empty child, joined by commas. Preorder plus null markers determines the tree uniquely. To deserialize, split on commas and consume tokens through an iterator: a marker gives None, otherwise create a node and recursively build its left subtree and then its right subtree. Both directions visit each node once: O(n) time and space.
